content:
The State of Texas has declared nine islands in the Rio Grande state property, a stretch the Texas General Land Office describes as spanning from Laredo to McAllen, according to the agency and news reports of its announcement.

Texas Land Commissioner Dawn Buckingham announced Oct. 26 that the General Land Office had identified the nine islands, totaling roughly 66 acres, as belonging to the State of Texas. The agency said the determination resolves uncertainty over jurisdiction and allows the Texas Department of Public Safety and the Texas Military Department to access, monitor and protect the islands.

The review followed a request from U.S. Customs and Border Protection concerning 28 islands whose ownership had not been established, according to reports of the announcement. The General Land Office said it used historical maps, topographical surveys, aerial photographs and geographic records to determine ownership.

Buckingham said state law enforcement partners were being notified so they could gain access to the islands to patrol, inspect and clear them of any illegal activity they encounter. In her letter to state agencies, she also acknowledged that criminal activity had not been confirmed on these additional islands, according to reports of the letter — a point the state framed as preventive, citing past experience with border islands being exploited by cartels and smugglers.

Mexico’s Foreign Ministry objected, according to El País reporting cited in later coverage. Mexico’s position is that the 1970 Treaty of Limits fixes the border to the river’s normal channel and that only the International Boundary and Water Commission can determine the international boundary and approve interventions — leaving the state’s claim legally disputed and unresolved as of this week.

The move builds on earlier island declarations by the same office: Fronton Island, a 170-acre island in Starr County, in 2023, and Roma and Bear islands, also in Starr County, afterward, according to the agency’s announcement.

Sources:

  • Texas General Land Office, “Texas Land Commissioner Buckingham Identifies Nine State-Owned Islands Along Texas-Mexico Border,” Oct. 26, 2026
  • Border Report, “Texas says 9 islands in Rio Grande belong to state, not Mexico,” Oct. 27, 2026
  • Sonora Presente / El País reporting, “Texas claims nine Rio Grande islands; Mexico demands border treaty be respected,” Oct. 30, 2026

Webb Watch 956
excerpt: The Texas General Land Office says nine Rio Grande islands totaling about 66 acres belong to the state and can now be patrolled by state forces; Mexico says only the binational boundary commission can settle island ownership.
title: Texas claims nine Rio Grande islands from Laredo to McAllen; Mexico protests, citing border treaty
